summary: T. Griffith Foulk works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (1978–1987) under Luis O. Gómez, later serving there as assistant professor (1987–1995) and at Sarah Lawrence College (1995–2005).
T. K. V. Desikachar (1938–2016) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied under Tirumalai Krishnamacharya from circa 1961 to 1989 and founded the Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram in 1976.

T. N. Ramachandran (1901–1973) was an archaeologist and Indologist. His career included posts as archaeologist at the Government Museum, Chennai (attested 1933) and curator of archaeology at the National Museum, New Delhi.

T. R. Chintamani was an Indologist who studied under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He served as Senior Lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Madras (~1930–1944) and as Manager and Correspondent for the Journal of Oriental Research.

T. R. V. Murti (1902–1986) worked in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. Supervised by Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, he earned a D.Litt. from Banaras Hindu University (~1945–1948), later holding professorships at BHU (~1953–1967) and McMaster University (~1970–1971).
T. S. Eliot (1888–1965) worked in philosophy and other fields. He studied under George Santayana and also studied under Charles Rockwell Lanman from 1911 to 1912.

T. S. Srinivasa Sastri was a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He held posts at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, attested in 1972 and later as Professor between 1984 and 1992.
T. Shrinivas Shastri is an Indology scholar affiliated with the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, where he is attested as Pandit in 1993 and as Professor in 2026.

T. V. Ramachandra Dikshitar was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as Principal of Madras Sanskrit College (attested 1938) and Professor of Advaita Vedānta at Banaras Hindu University (attested 1946).

T. V. Vasudeva is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. His career includes serving at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute as an Editorial Committee member (attested 2001) and as Deputy Director (attested 2026).

T. V. Venkatachala Sastry is a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Mysore under teachers including D. L. Narasimhachar and Harogadde Manappa Nayak. He held lecturing posts before becoming Professor at Mysore (1984–1994).

T. Venkatacharya was an Indologist and linguist. He held a post at the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East and was Professor of East Asian Studies at the University of Toronto (attested 1971).

Tadao Yoshikawa is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Kyoto University, later serving there as assistant professor (1974, 1984–2000), as professor at Ryukoku University (2002), and as president of Toho Gakkai (~2007–2011).

Tadashi Inoue (1929–2014) was a scholar of archaeology and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Tokyo, he held posts at the Kyoto National Museum, Iida City Museum (director, 1988–2006), Bukkyo University, and Kyoto University of the Arts.

Tadashi Sekino (1868–1935) was a scholar in archaeology, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1892 to 1895 and later served there as Professor Emeritus from circa 1929 to 1935.

Tadashi Tani is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed doctoral studies at Waseda University (~1972–1977), studied under Yuichi Kajiyama at Kyoto University, and served as professor at Kochi College (~1989–2006).
Tadashi Toda is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Keiki Higashimoto and Kogen Mizuno.

Tadeusz Skorupski is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who earned his PhD from the University of London (by 1978). He spent his academic career at SOAS University of London, serving as Professor and Reader.
Tai-shing Wut is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Ming-Wood Liu (attested 1998).

Taichiro Kobayashi (1901–1963) studied Sinology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies at Kyoto University under Sentaro Sawamura and others. He worked at the Eastern Cultural Institute, Osaka City Museum of Fine Arts, and as professor at Kobe University (1950).
